findings.title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
findings.body: The fourth `Objects.requireNonNull` call checks `grantType` a second time but uses the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed". As a result `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null raw id is silently accepted, and `encodeTokenId` would then produce an id such as `onrtac:null` instead of failing fast. It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong indices and inverted condition
findings.body: The grant shortcut sits at characters 4-6 of the prefix, so it should be read with `substring(4, 6)`. The matcher reads `substring(3, 5)` instead; for `onrtac` that yields `ta`. The condition is also inverted: it returns false when the value equals the expected shortcut. With both errors the check effectively never rejects anything, so the matcher only verifies the `prefix:UUID` shape. The integration tests therefore do not verify that the correct grant type is encoded in the token id. Use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type providers
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added to a public SPI interface without a default implementation. Existing custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations will no longer compile. Already-built extension jars will hit `AbstractMethodError` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, and that failure aborts server startup. A shortcut that returns null would also throw an NPE when inserted into the `ConcurrentHashMap`. Consider adding a default implementation, or handling missing or null shortcuts gracefully.

findings.title: Javadoc says '3-letters' shortcut but encoder requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc tells implementors the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters". However, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` decodes the context by assuming exactly 2 characters per segment and rejects any prefix whose length is not 6. A custom grant following the doc with a 3-character shortcut would get tokens issued successfully (encoding does not validate length), and those tokens could never be decoded by `getTokenContextFromTokenId`. Fix the documentation to require exactly 2 characters, and validate the shortcut length at registration time.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
findings.body: The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor was deleted from the server-spi-private `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Any extension or subclass using it will break. The removal is unrelated to the feature. It could instead have been kept and extended to copy the new `grantType` field.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes due to NPE rather than validation
findings.body: In this test the factory's `sessionFactory` is never set, so it is null. For the unknown shortcut `ac`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls back to `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws a `NullPointerException`. The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes because of that NPE rather than because of the intended `IllegalArgumentException` for an unknown grant type. Assert the specific exception type, or mock the session factory.
